feature: Page-tree traversal, page order, node/page identity, and counts
source_location: Processed EC3 md lines 3119–3151; Table 30 printed p.103. A conforming processor shall handle any page-tree shape built from page and Pages nodes. Kids determine descendants/order; Count is required and producer shall make it consistent. A node may not be multiply referenced; a page object may not be multiply referenced.
errata: No directly applicable EC3 change to Tables 30/31 traversal requirements found. Do not turn required Type/Parent/Kids/Count producer entries into mandatory reader rejection behavior.
code: pdf-model/src/page.rs::Pages::new/get/Walk; limits for maximum depth and visited nodes; damaged-tree scan recovery is separate fallback behavior.
test_assertions: Tests assert exact page count/order/geometry for valid non-flat trees, query/index consistency, and separate malformed-tree recovery/reporting. Several malformed nodes test project recovery policy; required Table 30 fields are writer constraints, so their specific recovery outcomes are policy rather than ISO reader obligations.
verdict: SUPPORTED for common non-flat/unbalanced traversal and selected damage paths; not a proof over every possible tree shape or resource bound.
residuals: Depth and million-node limits are implementation safety bounds, not source-specified numerical requirements. Duplicate page/node references are producer violations; do not infer that the reader must reject rather than choose a deterministic traversal.

feature: Page attributes: inherited fields, nearest-value shadowing, no merge, defaults, and non-inheritable fields
source_location: Processed EC3 md lines 3152–3260; Table 31 printed p.104 onward. Only Resources, MediaBox, CropBox and Rotate are inheritable. Nearest ancestor wins; inherited values are used as-is, including complete arrays/dictionaries rather than merged pieces. Optional inherited attributes fall back to their own stated default if no ancestor supplies them; a required one must exist on page or ancestor. Linearized-PDF conformance adds a writer obligation that all attributes appear on page dictionaries.
errata: EC3 #106/#619 amend Table31 /ID only (indirect-reference preference struck; PDF 2.0 deprecation inserted), unrelated to drawing/inheritance. Annex F linearization is audited separately by parent; its explicit-attribute rule is not an ordinary reader error mandate.
ledger: Rows 7.7.3.3 and 7.7.3.4 (implemented); connected page geometry §14.11.2 rows are separate owners for clipping/boundary behavior.
code: pdf-model/src/page.rs::Inherited::overlay/build_page and rectangle/rotation/resource selection; page_geometry.rs reads CropBox, Rotate, UserUnit and media-box reports.
test_assertions: Direct model tests prove nearest Resources dictionary and empty-dictionary shadowing; geometry test proves inherited MediaBox and Rotate while ancestor UserUnit is not inherited; invalid local MediaBox test checks documented policy. Existing page-runtime resource test exercises one parent level. Draft `drafts/inherited_resources_render.rs` adds a root-vs-intermediate same-name XObject public-output test; unrun.
verdict: SUPPORTED for nearest whole-dictionary Resources, empty shadow, Rotate/MediaBox inheritance, and one non-inheritable field; sampled test evidence, not all four inheritable fields at all depths.
residuals: No reviewed test asserts inherited CropBox through the real renderer, or a page-local CropBox overriding an intermediate node's CropBox in public painted output. Draft closes Resources consumer gap only. Missing/bad required fields and malformed non-inheritable entries need not produce a prescribed reader error unless another clause states one.

feature: Page Contents cardinality, absent/null/invalid values, arrays as one stream, separators, and total decode bounds
source_location: Processed EC3 md lines 3152–3178 and 3265–3301; Table 31 printed p.104 onward. Contents is optional; absent page is empty; null is equivalent to absent under §7.3.9. Array effect is stream parts in order joined with at least one whitespace byte. Writers may split only at lexical-token boundaries and shall not create an empty Contents array. Consumer need not preserve the array structure. §7.8.3's old phrase explicitly naming a page Contents array was struck by EC3 #9 because §7.8.2 already treats it as one stream.
errata: EC3 #9 strikes “(or is an element of an array that is the value of that entry)” from §7.8.3’s page-resource bullet; it does not revoke array concatenation. §7.8.2 and Table31 still govern it. No new reader obligation to preserve the input parts exists.
ledger: Rows 7.7.3.3 and 7.8.2, both implemented; content reader limits are local safety policy attached to the single-stream model.
code: pdf-model/src/page.rs::content_with_report and content/reader.rs::ContentReader/Window; per-part decoding plus synthetic whitespace and bound on total decoded bytes.
test_assertions: The deflated two-part test puts path operands in the first stream and operator in the second, then checks both commands/no issues; hostile-budget test asserts no report and a command from parts spanning the join. This directly discriminates the required inter-part whitespace. Entry tests distinguish absent/null, unreachable, nonstream, empty valid stream, and indexed partial loss. `max_stream_len` is project bound, justified by concatenation being one stream; numerical limit is not ISO-specified.
verdict: STRONGLY SUPPORTED for array order/separator, cross-part interpretation, absent/null, and per-part issue reporting.
residuals: The only required producer distinction is that an empty Contents array shall not be emitted; malformed zero-element array recovery is not a mandatory-reader error rule. Test names cited do not prove preservation of original array boundaries, which is expressly unnecessary.

feature: Content stream operands, sequential lexing, compatibility operators, and resource dictionary association
source_location: Processed EC3 md lines 3261–3342; §7.8.3 printed p.127. Content instructions execute sequentially; operands are direct objects before operators; BX/EX bracket ignoring unknown operators. Resource names are local to each stream, and dictionaries enumerate resources used. Table34 categories include ExtGState, ColorSpace, Pattern, Shading, XObject, Font, deprecated ProcSet, Properties.
errata: EC3 #128 replaces the Type3 glyph resources rule with four-step lookup: glyph stream's own Resources, Type3 font Resources, page dictionary, then inherited page resources. It retires old broad fallback wording to NOTE 3. EC3 #9 removes redundant explicit mention of array members. #47/#48 strike standard-14 font processor support sentence in §9.6.2.2; relevant only to cross-clause predefined-font fallback, not Table34 itself.
ledger: Rows 7.8.1, 7.8.2, 7.8.3 (implemented); Table34 ProcSet is separately treated as deprecated/advisory and inapplicable in this screen reader.
code: pdf-model/src/content/run.rs and content/reader.rs; content/resources.rs resource_entry; content/xobject.rs; type3.rs::Type3Font::resources; pattern/appearance and soft-mask callers.
test_assertions: Each-stream same-name test checks red page control, green form target, red restored page control; inherited page resource test checks a blue display-list fill; byte-distinct names test checks three color sequence values. Type3 test covers EC3 #128's new first lookup step. Missing-resource tests cover page fallback versus own resources and nested fallback. Findings/report tests are project diagnostic policy when resource names are missing; a producer's missing named resource does not imply ISO mandates this reader's exact error message.
verdict: SUPPORTED for resource dictionary identity/scope, page inheritance into execution, and EC3 Type3 lookup correction; broad Table34 category completeness was not recertified here.
residuals: New draft composes multiple page-tree inheritance levels with actual drawing. Search order for malformed Type3 glyph streams is exercised on its new first step; every fallback step is represented in broader tests but not exhaustively re-proved in this bounded pass. Exact diagnostics for invalid resource dictionary shapes are policy unless an operator/table explicitly requires the missing operand to be named.
